title: section-b — `core/Section`: a sub page that starts empty and picks an approved layout (Opus)

set.request: core/Section: a sub page that starts empty and picks an approved layout. Section extends Page; starts as a default div with min-height 2.5em; editing off by default, turned on by code; one hover control picks an approved core/Layout that FITS the section's live width; picking applies the layout, its slots become regions, children mount by name. Demos never persist. Page at /framework/core/Section/, registered in core/page.js.
steps: Read the brief, the plan, core/Layout, core/Page
Section.js - the class, the overlay, the picker, the slots
page.js - one screen showing all three states
Register Section in core/page.js and css-scopes.txt
ui-test: overlay, fitting counts at 400 and 3440, slots, reload
Crawl core/, core/Page/, core/Layout/ - zero new errors
set.outcome:
**`core/Section` lands — a page you put inside a page, that picks an approved layout.**

[The page](/framework/core/Section/) is one screen and three demos: an empty section with editing on (hover it — a hairline and one control, and nothing moves), the same section with two children mounted into `main-aside`'s slots by name, and a third read off disk from a `page.json`.

![](stacked-390.png)

**What it is.** `Section extends Page`, so storage (`store()`, keyed on its own url), children, naming, regions and the six page words all arrive inherited — the only new prop is `layout`, the name of an entry in [core/Layout](/framework/core/Layout/). Empty it is a `min-height: 2.5em` div with no class, no padding and no chrome; `editing: true` (or `section.edit()`, called by a demo or doc page, never by a visitor) adds a dashed hairline and one corner control.

**The picker is `ext/Dropdown`, subclassed — not copied.** It lists only the approved layouts that FIT this box, read off its live width: **21 of 30 pickable at 1280** (899px box), **30 at 1920 and 3440**, **0 at 400** (276px box — the narrowest floor on the site is 400). A layout below the floor is not an option at all but a row saying `needs 1000px — this box is 899px`; when nothing fits, the list says which layout is narrowest and that the box is already the stack.

**LayoutRule #1 has a second half the picker cannot cover:** a section *handed* a layout and then viewed narrow. `main-aside` in a 276px box drew **4,433px of column**. It now stacks below its floor — a `ResizeObserver` re-asks on every width change and the overlay says `stacked — Main + aside needs 700px`. Press MOBILE on the second demo to watch it happen.

**Docs:** [Idea](/framework/core/Section/doc/idea/) · [Picker](/framework/core/Section/doc/picker/) · [Slots](/framework/core/Section/doc/slots/) · `readme.md`. Registered in `core/page.js` `children:` and `styles/css-scopes.txt` (`page-section-`).

**Proven:** zero console errors at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440, no sideways scroll, no box overflowing its own width; the empty section measures 37.6px = exactly 2.5em; pick → slots appear → reload → the choice is gone and `localStorage` holds nothing (demos do not persist); `/framework/core/`, `core/Page/`, `core/Layout/` and the three notes all crawl clean at 1280.

**Two findings for files outside this task's fence, logged above:** `Page.from()` says `new Page(…)` in the middle, so no subclass can inherit it (`new this(…)` would fix it for all of them); and **a page whose `content` is a plain string renders it as an anonymous grid item** — `.page > *` cannot reach it, so it lands in the gutter track and sets one character per line (a 40-word paragraph drew 4,766px at 1280, no error). Any `page.json` with `mode.content` as text hits it.

**Left deliberately:** `fits()` lives in `Section.js` and belongs in `core/Layout` (fenced); no `saves:` flag — nothing sets it yet, and only an editor should; a fallback with meaningful slots would want `drawn()` revisited (all sixteen name `stack` or `rows` today).
